questions.question: What color do you get when you mix red and yellow?
questions.explanation: Red and yellow are primary colors that make orange when mixed together!
questions.funFact: Carrots used to be purple or white before farmers selectively bred them to be orange!

questions.question: What tool is usually used to put paint on a canvas?
questions.explanation: A paintbrush has bristles that help spread paint smoothly.
questions.funFact: The oldest known paintbrushes are about 2.5 million years old and were made of animal hair!

questions.question: What color do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
questions.explanation: Mixing the primary colors blue and yellow creates the secondary color green.
questions.funFact: The human eye can see more shades of green than any other color!

questions.question: What do we call a painting or drawing of a person's face?
questions.explanation: A portrait is a piece of art that focuses on a person's face and expression.
questions.funFact: Before cameras were invented, people would sit completely still for hours to have their portrait painted!

questions.question: What squishy material can you shape with your hands to make a sculpture?
questions.explanation: Clay is soft when wet and can be molded into many shapes before it dries.
questions.funFact: Some ancient clay pots that have been found are over 20,000 years old!

questions.question: What do you wear over your clothes to keep them clean while painting?
questions.explanation: A smock or apron covers your regular clothes so paint doesn't ruin them.
questions.funFact: Many famous painters used old, oversized shirts as their smocks!

questions.question: Which of these is an instrument with black and white keys?
questions.explanation: A piano makes music when you press its black and white keys.
questions.funFact: A standard piano has exactly 88 keys—52 white ones and 36 black ones!

questions.question: What do we call art made by folding paper into fun shapes?
questions.explanation: Origami is the traditional Japanese art of folding paper.
questions.funFact: The traditional origami crane is a symbol of peace, and folding 1,000 of them is said to grant a wish!

questions.question: What building do you visit to look at famous paintings and sculptures?
questions.explanation: A museum is a special place where art is kept safe and shown to the public.
questions.funFact: The biggest art museum in the world is the Louvre in Paris, and it would take 100 days to see everything inside it!

questions.question: What happens when you mix red and white paint?
questions.explanation: Adding white to red makes it lighter, creating the color pink.
questions.funFact: In the past, pink was actually considered a color for boys, and blue was for girls!

questions.question: What object does an artist hold to keep their paints in one place?
questions.explanation: A palette is a flat board used for holding and mixing different colors of paint.
questions.funFact: Some artists use palettes made of glass so they can scrape the dry paint off easily!

questions.question: What do you do at the end of a play to show the actors you liked it?
questions.explanation: Clapping, or applause, is how an audience says 'good job' to performers.
questions.funFact: In some countries, clapping in perfect rhythm together is a sign of ultimate respect for the performers!

questions.question: What kind of art is made by gluing different pieces of paper and pictures together?
questions.explanation: A collage is created by assembling different materials, like magazines or colored paper, onto a flat surface.
questions.funFact: The word 'collage' comes from a French word that means 'to glue'!

questions.question: What do we call a picture taken with a camera?
questions.explanation: Cameras capture light to create a permanent image called a photograph.
questions.funFact: The first photograph ever taken took 8 hours to finish!

questions.question: Which of these sticks is used to draw pictures on the sidewalk?
questions.explanation: Chalk is a soft, powdery stick perfect for drawing on rough surfaces like sidewalks.
questions.funFact: Natural chalk is actually made from the tiny shells of ancient sea creatures!

questions.question: What do we call someone who pretends to be a character in a movie or play?
questions.explanation: An actor's job is to act out a story for an audience.
questions.funFact: The first known actor was a man from ancient Greece named Thespis!

questions.question: What do ballet dancers wear on their feet?
questions.explanation: Ballet dancers wear special soft slippers to help them move gracefully.
questions.funFact: Professional ballet dancers can go through 2 to 3 pairs of ballet slippers in just one week!

questions.question: What do we call a very quick, messy drawing?
questions.explanation: A sketch is a rough, quick drawing artists do to practice their ideas.
questions.funFact: Many famous artists carried a small sketchpad with them everywhere they went!

questions.question: What type of art is a movie you watch on a big screen?
questions.explanation: Cinema, or filmmaking, is the art of telling stories with moving pictures and sound.
questions.funFact: The first movies ever made didn't have any sound or color!

questions.question: What is the very first shape you learn to draw that looks like the sun?
questions.explanation: A circle is perfectly round and is often used to draw the sun, faces, and wheels.
questions.funFact: There are no straight lines at all in a true circle!
